method: Nine code readers, one per core subsystem, read the implementation and ran reproductions. Every finding was adversarially verified: two independent lenses (reproduce; scope/reachability) for P0/P1, one otherwise; a finding survives with a majority of real votes. 109 found, 106 survived, 3 refuted. The 106 were deduplicated into 75 problems (R-01..R-75) and 30 improvements (I-01..I-31, I-17 absorbed into I-08) by a synthesis agent over all 106, checked by a completeness critic: every finding maps to exactly one problem, every problem is addressed, risk and gain shares sum to 100. R-01, R-03 and R-10 were additionally reproduced by hand at the audited commit.

share_rules.risk_share_pct: weight = severity (P0 8, P1 5, P2 3, P3 1.5) x reach (production entry point 1.5; library default path or committed evidence 1.0-1.3; library-only non-default 0.8; needs record forgery 0.6) x likelihood (ordinary data/defaults 1.2; plausible 1.0; specific structure 0.8; contrived 0.6), normalised to 100
share_rules.goal_gain_pct: share of the remaining gap to a core whose claims are never stronger than its evidence, whose guards production reaches, and which can be certified as Core Freeze V4; normalised to 100
share_rules.stars: problems: 5 = P0, 4 = P1, 3 = P2, 2 = bounded P3, 1 = hygiene; improvements: importance to the goal

reach_map: The MCP server is the main production entry point. It exposes describe_capabilities, run_electrothermal and run_battery, which go through problem and battery case runners into CredibilityEvidenceReport and derive_verdict, so the results, validation and credibility guards are reached there. On that path the verdict block never shows evidence_basis, and the report ignores convergence, uncertainty and declared validity requirements. record_values is never passed, so the CORE-014 operating-point binding does not fire (R-04, R-09, R-10, R-72). Domain runners reach conduction2d boundary handling (R-56), the electrothermal coupling with bare-value transfers (R-58), and multirotor design archives that rank unassessed candidates (R-44). The only production calibration route is studies/calibration_study and the battery B1-B3 tables. They run through frozen V1 gaussian_grid_posterior, posterior_predictive_uq and assess_predictive_observation, so no V2 goodness-of-fit, containment, uniqueness or prediction-domain gate runs (R-02, R-35, R-36, R-38). engcore.hybrid_uq, adequacy comparison, TrustedConsensusGate, Experiment.best, the oracles and uq admission have no production caller; benchmarks, audits and certification tools reach them only as a library. The certification tools themselves are latent: they certify the live API with no additive-only comparator, accept self-asserted assurance, and leave the batch guards outside the pinned mutation population (R-65 to R-70). Until I-03, I-11 and I-16 land, most V2 fixes lower library risk without sitting between a production entry point and a published number.

problems.title: A grid rebuild turns an unassessed or incomplete uniqueness search into a SUPPORTED one-mode grid
problems.brief: With the default multistart=None, the local route is DOWNGRADED for GLOBAL_UNIQUENESS_NOT_ASSESSED, but step 3 rebuilds a SUPPORTED grid around that one estimate anyway. It misses a mode holding 63% of the posterior (sd 42x too small in the prior repro).

problems.title: Observations that carry no information dilute the pooled goodness-of-fit gate (CORE-001)
problems.brief: The chi2 test pools every residual on n-p dof. A REFUSED misfit (chi2/dof 9) becomes SUPPORTED once 60-1000 uninformative observations are added, and its covariance does not change.

problems.title: A supplied grid over one of two equal modes is SUPPORTED, and a caller's MultistartPolicy is never run
problems.brief: Step 1 returns GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED before multistart runs, and it tests only the box faces. The same request through local_gaussian_posterior with MultistartPolicy() is REFUSED with SECOND_MODE_FOUND.

problems.title: The V1 grid resolution check fits one quadratic about the top node, so an unresolved second mode inside the box passes
problems.brief: _fitted_lattice_covariance fits only at the argmax, with no residual test. A narrow second mode (local sd 0.00065 at step 0.005) is SUPPORTED with an sd about 14x too small.

problems.title: Multistart dismisses a converged refit in another basin as WORSE_LOCAL_OPTIMUM on peak height alone
problems.brief: A separated optimum is classified by objective value only, and the verdict ignores WORSE_LOCAL_OPTIMUM. A broad basin holding most of the mass is dropped, and the SUPPORTED 95% interval holds 17.7% of the posterior.

problems.title: Adequacy content binding omits split identity, likelihood sigma and twin, so compare pairs assessments that do not belong together
problems.brief: compare_log_predictive_scores pairs identical models calibrated on different data under one dataset-id label and gives a decisive preference (delta -5.8, se 0.86). A caller-chosen sigma (0.05 K vs declared 0.5 K) creates a preference, and a twin mismatch still reads content_bound=True.

problems.title: A verification-only SUPPORTED reads bare in the MCP verdict block, and verification levels need no issuer
problems.area: mcp server verdict block / results validation
problems.brief: Every SUPPORTED MCP verdict is VERIFICATION_ONLY, but evidence_basis appears only in the nested report and the block shows no reasons. A hand-written ANALYTICALLY_VERIFIED check with evidence 'trust me' turns INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE into SUPPORTED and survives from_dict.

problems.title: The CORE-014 operating-point binding never fires in production and is bypassable when enabled
problems.brief: record_values has no caller, assess_validity cannot forward it, and the MCP report path merges validity without comparing. An IN_DOMAIN assessment made at one operating point is accepted for a result at another (alpha -1e-5 vs 1e-5 reads SUPPORTED). When enabled, it matches by name only and drops evaluated on read.

problems.title: The production calibration study predicts and validates through frozen V1 functions, so no V2 evidence gate runs
problems.brief: posterior_predictive_uq and assess_predictive_observation apply no goodness-of-fit, containment, prior or domain check. A box of mean +/-0.6 sd truncates the posterior sd to 0.34x and is still content-bound and usable for a decisive comparison.

problems.title: The credibility report never reads result convergence
problems.brief: A DIVERGED, MAX_ITERATIONS or FAILED result with a passing check derives SUPPORTED, and convergence is absent from the report JSON, even though is_usable is False.

problems.title: ScientificProblem validation_requirements and UncertaintySpecification are declared but enforced nowhere
problems.brief: The DC, CSTR and conduction problems declare required checks that nothing reads. from_dict silently drops misspelled keys, so a requirement like 'numerically_convergd' is accepted and never checked.

problems.title: The minimum-search rule ignores max_evaluations and maximum_retractions, and failed refits are dropped
problems.brief: A refit budget of 12 evaluations turns REFUSED SECOND_MODE_FOUND into SUPPORTED, as long as half the starts converge. The committed K2 kinetics evidence relies on this search.

problems.title: evidence_basis labels agreement between two solvers of the same declared model as VALIDATED
problems.brief: CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED is in VALIDATION_LEVELS, so native plus ngspice agreement on one DCCircuit declaration reads VALIDATED. That is verification of one model, not validation against reality.

problems.title: require_complete_boundary checks one condition per region id, not per edge
problems.brief: If two conditions share a region id, the last one wins in conduction2d. A declared Dirichlet edge is silently dropped while every completeness and Dirichlet check passes.

problems.title: A posterior cut at the declared upper bound, with data bounding only the lower side, is SUPPORTED
problems.brief: Domination is refused only when both sides truncate. Moving the upper bound from 20 to 40 to 80 changes the reported sd from 1.74 to 2.04 to 3.47, all SUPPORTED, so the bound sets the answer.

problems.title: calibration_observations for a routed prediction are bound to nothing
problems.brief: Passing another dataset's observations, rescaled conditions or a predictor evaluated elsewhere silences PREDICTION_OUTSIDE_CALIBRATED_CONDITIONS. A far extrapolation (x=1e4) reads SUPPORTED although the posterior carries its own dataset_id.

problems.title: Probe directions come from eigh(cov) in declared units, so a unit change moves the tested directions
problems.brief: The same model and data are SUPPORTED with a parameter in volts and REFUSED (TAIL_HEAVIER_THAN_LOCAL_GAUSSIAN) in millivolts.

problems.title: CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED is guarded only by string checks, and non-independent disagreement is absorbed as WARNING
problems.brief: Hand-written consensus evidence lines earn the level and survive a result round trip, and TrustedConsensusGate has no caller. Routes 33% apart that are not verified independent give WARNING, and the verdict stays SUPPORTED.

problems.title: The prediction-domain gate compares only the conditions the prediction chooses to declare
problems.brief: Calibration held T=300 K. A prediction at T=900 K is DOWNGRADED, but the same prediction with T omitted is SUPPORTED. Joint-support departures (0.71 off the calibrated line) also pass.

problems.title: Split duplicate handling: replicates within a half inflate n, and near-duplicates cross into held-out
problems.brief: One held-out reading listed four times gives n=4, se=0 and a decisive preference. A calibration reading re-imported at 4-8 significant digits, with a re-declared sigma or a renamed observable, is accepted as held-out.

problems.title: The decisive-comparison gate uses a normal 2 SE critical value with an SE from n-1 dof
problems.brief: Between mirror-image models, a preferred model is named in 27.5% of runs at n=2 and 19.3% at n=3.

problems.title: Linearized predictive nonlinearity is never refused and is pooled across specs
problems.brief: A prediction with nonlinearity=inf and parameter sd 0 is still emitted, only DOWNGRADED. One quadratic output also downgrades an exactly affine prediction in the same call and records inf as its nonlinearity.

problems.title: Experiment.best judges feasibility from whatever checks a candidate carries
problems.brief: Declared constraints need not be checked, and checks are not tied to the result's numbers. A candidate that checks one of two constraints is feasible, and from_dict without a constraints key drops them, changing best from eval-1 to eval-2.

problems.title: UncertaintySource never reaches a verdict or report, and SRIA budgets accept NUMERICAL as model-form
problems.brief: source_kind has no producer, and the report has no uncertainty field. The SRIA budget marks aleatoric and model_form 'known' from a numerical-only record.

problems.title: Spreads on offset temperature scales convert as absolute temperatures
problems.area: units in oracles, constraints, grid, split
problems.brief: A '0.5 degC' tolerance becomes 273.65 K, so a prediction of 573 K passes against 300 K. Sigmas and tolerances in degC become about 274 K, while the correct delta_degC form crashes.

problems.title: The corner-agreement guard compares magnitudes in each law's own unit
problems.brief: 300 K meeting 300 degC (573 K) is accepted, a 273 K conflict at the corner. 300 K meeting 26.85 degC, the same temperature, is refused.

problems.title: Forward-model admission is not bound to the source result, and tables bind observations by key label only
problems.brief: The analytic admission route skips convergence and the source result's validation, so a 2-cell, 1-step solve is admitted. AdmittedForwardTable accepts any strings as admission refs and compares data in the observation's own unit (1500 milliohm against a 1.5 ohm table).

problems.title: The 3 and 6 sd tail probes run only along principal axes
problems.brief: A posterior flat along the diagonals beyond 3 sd is SUPPORTED, and its 95% intervals hold 76.8% of the marginal (mass beyond radius 3 is 0.20, against 0.011 for a Gaussian).

problems.title: A tail probe beyond a declared bound is skipped without being counted
problems.brief: The same flat-tailed posterior is REFUSED with bounds at 6.01 sd and SUPPORTED at 5.99 sd.

problems.title: A posterior cut by forward-model inadmissibility counts as contained
problems.brief: Faces with no admissible node read as empty, so supplied grids cut at an inadmissibility boundary are SUPPORTED with means off by up to 0.57 sd.

problems.title: assess_routed_identifiability accepts loosened thresholds on the local route
problems.brief: The INF-10 declared-or-tighter guard runs only for grids. Canonical NOT_IDENTIFIABLE (correlation 0.9999985) becomes WEAKLY_IDENTIFIABLE under caller thresholds, and the record reads back.

problems.title: A provenance override in from_result drops declared but unassessed models
problems.brief: Passing a provenance that names only one of the result's two models turns INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE into SUPPORTED, with unassessed=().

problems.title: The objective-versus-result check is keyed by objective name, not metric
problems.brief: When the name differs from the metric, the check is skipped. best() ranks on objective 0.001 W while the result carries load = 50 W.

problems.title: Predictive-admission conditioning accepts any budget and returns an unmarked PosteriorGrid
problems.brief: With budget 1.0 it conditions away 99.9997% of the posterior (factor 3.4e5). The result reuses the original dataset_id and mask, so nothing downstream can tell.

problems.title: The pairwise +/-2 sd probes cannot see a curvature error spread over many pairs
problems.brief: Each axis and diagonal is checked alone within 0.1. At p=10 the claim is SUPPORTED while one direction's true sd is 2.24x the reported sd.

problems.title: Retracted multistart starts count as full-span starts
problems.brief: Starts the forward model refuses are halved toward the estimate (for example 12 becomes 0.75). With 5 of 6 retracted into one basin, the search reads MULTISTART_NO_SECOND_MODE, SUPPORTED, and misses an equal second mode.

problems.title: Evidence binding spot-checks 8 nodes, 4 of them seeded from the supplier's bytes
problems.brief: A grid with 5022 of 19881 nodes sharpened 4x passes after 2 grinding attempts and reports sd halved (0.0136 against 0.0272).

problems.title: Local RouteDiagnostics read-back trusts carried fields
problems.brief: Editing the observation count turns DOWNGRADED into SUPPORTED. A relabelled SECOND_MODE refit, stripped policy keys, or a record with no tail probe evaluated (NaN ratio) also reads SUPPORTED.

problems.title: Cross-domain crossings carry bare point values, and UncertaintyTransfer binds nothing
problems.brief: Production electrothermal coupling passes values with no uncertainty, validity or validation state. The unused UncertaintyTransfer accepts any same-dimension uncertainty, intervals that do not contain the value (350 K with 10-11 K), and overwritten attribution.

problems.title: HELD_OUT_VALIDATION_PASS is issued for any n>=1 with no power floor
problems.brief: Only PASS and FAIL exist, with FAIL at p<0.01. A misspecified model with one held-out point (residual 2.1 sd) passes in 24 of 40 seeds.

problems.title: The TCR held-out study refuses heterogeneous declared sigmas, and coverage repetitions claim CONVERGED without a calibration run
problems.brief: Held-out sigmas [0.002, 0.002, 0.003] can never be validated, because either observation_sigma is refused. Coverage records say CONVERGED although no calibration ran.

problems.title: CrossLimitCondition reports a missing declaration as a core gap
problems.brief: When one operand is supplied, RATED_LINEAR_TCR_MODEL reads UNREADABLE_SHAPE. Repair guidance tells the user that declaring it again will not help, which is wrong.

problems.title: Quantity.parse evaluates unit expressions, magnitudes accept bool or str, and delta units pass as absolute
problems.brief: At the MCP boundary, '5 volt 2' is accepted as 10 V and '2 volt + 3 volt' as 5 V. An ambient of '27 delta_degC' passes the dimension-only check as an absolute temperature.

problems.title: Batch-guard mutation evidence sits outside the pinned harness and counts any failure as a kill
problems.brief: None of the 44 batch guards is in MUTATIONS, two recorded kills (B1j, B1k) no longer apply, and several fix guards have no mutation. The runners mutate the shared checkout in place and treat any non-zero exit as KILLED.

problems.title: The uniform-prior step tolerance refuses a grid that is effectively uniform
problems.brief: A natural linspace grid on a LOG axis (step deviation 2%) is PASSED_OVER, although its mean and sd match the accepted log-linspace grid to 6 digits.

problems.title: The coverage verdict pools correlated intervals as independent trials
problems.brief: With ICC 0.37 (design effect 2.09), the Wilson interval is about 1.45x too narrow, and UNCERTAINTY_CALIBRATED verdicts flip near the band edges.

problems.title: Unassessed candidates are ranked: best() admits NOT_RUN validation and design archives lack the CORE-015 rule
problems.brief: best() picks a candidate with validation NOT_RUN and nothing attained. The multirotor Pareto and elite archives rank validity_not_assessed candidates as ELIGIBLE, and best() has no caller.

problems.title: The branch descends from no Core Freeze, and recertification is blocked
problems.brief: The V1 and V2 frozen digests moved (c80e6418 to 7a481264) and 4 API snapshot tests fail. The certificate-child self-check list makes recertification impossible without a V4 control-plane change.

problems.title: With 1 or 2 residual dof the variance-ratio refusal can never fire
problems.brief: The p>=0.01 check returns before the ratio test, so chi2/dof of 6.6 (dof 1) and 4.57 (dof 2) read SUPPORTED.

problems.title: POORLY_SCALED_PARAMETERIZATION is judged on the unit-dependent raw condition number
problems.brief: Declaring a slope in nanovolts instead of volts (raw condition 3.2e9, equilibrated 3.47) downgrades an exactly Gaussian result.

problems.title: The CORE-013 status precedence changed without a schema bump
problems.brief: Older validation_report/1 records with a NOT_RUN check are refused as tampered. SRIA reports 'validation never run' when a check simply did not apply, and older readers silently drop new bindings (evaluated, source_kind).

problems.title: GUARD 21 compares signed residual and tolerance
problems.brief: A PASS with residual -10 against tolerance 1e-6, or with a negative tolerance, is constructed and earns NUMERICALLY_CONVERGED.

problems.title: Validity condition primitives accept declarations whose meaning silently inverts
problems.brief: allowed='laminar' becomes the letter set, so 'laminar' is outside the domain and 'a' is in it. Ratio bounds with a > b still read in_domain.

problems.title: Mesh identity depends on unit-conversion float rounding and a 1e-12 m floor
problems.brief: 7 mm and 0.7 cm get different fingerprints, and 10 nm against 10.0005 nm reads as the same geometry at two resolutions, so transfers wrongly require projection.

problems.title: The energy-crossing guard matches only exact energy or power dimensions
problems.brief: W/m^2, W/m, J/kg and W/m^3 cross with no declared EnergyConversion, while plain watt is refused.

problems.title: The frozen API snapshot cannot see method-level contracts or additive-only violations
problems.brief: Removing record_values or evidence_basis leaves the V1 and V2 digests unchanged. v1_entries_byte_identical_in_v2 compares live to live, and 13 RouteReason members changed position without detection.

problems.title: An evidence-binding mismatch raises instead of passing over
problems.brief: A grid off only at solver-tolerance level (chi-square 1064.66 on both sides) aborts route_uncertainty with HybridUQError. The same request without the grid is LOCAL_GAUSSIAN SUPPORTED.

problems.title: The consensus verdict depends on route order through the first route's unit
problems.brief: Relative difference is taken on offset-scale magnitudes in the first route's unit. Swapping route order changes 3.7e-9 (disagree) to 3.3e-10 (CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED).

problems.title: Field validity decides from an unbound self-declared summary and a component envelope
problems.brief: FieldSummary is never checked against the bytes or unit, so a forged summary reads in_domain with the same reference digest. A 3-component field with |u|=1.73 passes a 1.2 m/s maximum.

problems.title: The QuantityTransfer conversion budget check has a 1.0 absolute floor
problems.brief: Small crossings in large exemplar units (1 mW with gigawatt) report 100% arrival against a declared 50% efficiency and are accepted.

problems.title: content_bound is a caller-settable flag that the decisive comparison treats as proof
problems.brief: from_dict or replace with content_bound=True yields a decisive preference (15.9 nats), even with fabricated log densities. The comparison has no production caller.

problems.title: Oracle operating-point conditions are the caller's word, partial and optional
problems.brief: compare never checks where the prediction was computed. Observations without conditions pass at a stated T=9999 K.

problems.title: A result accepts an IN_DOMAIN assessment over conditions its model does not have
problems.brief: Condition names are checked only at the MCP boundary. Core consumers (experiments, admissibility) trust satisfied=('anything_at_all',).

problems.title: Oracle comparison fails an unpredicted metric and cannot compare multi-point evidence
problems.brief: A missing metric scores FAIL rather than NOT_RUN. An evidence set at T=300 K and 400 K is NOT_RUN for every stated point.

problems.title: FieldObservationOperator binds its region by label and snaps out-of-support probes to an edge
problems.brief: Any region with a matching id is applied, and the digest excludes region content. A probe outside the mesh silently reads the nearest edge node.

problems.title: Grid-route predictions ignore predict and never check the predictive table's values
problems.brief: A table of twice the model, passed with the correct predict(), gives a SUPPORTED mean of 3.949 against the honest 1.975.

problems.title: Renaming the parameterization or moving recorded bounds escapes the HUQ-12 bound-distance check
problems.brief: A forged 'linear_map:' record, or bounds moved with the covariance, lets a 100x narrower covariance read back SUPPORTED, alone and inside a HybridUQResult.

problems.title: Grid HybridUQResult read-back and prediction trust hand-built records
problems.brief: Variance divided by 5 to 7, or covariance /100 with widths /10, an identifiability flip and an impossible rebuild record all read back SUPPORTED. A hand-built result around a grid that failed evidence predicts a SUPPORTED mean of 2.47 against 1.97.

problems.title: The V2 and V3 freeze verifiers accept a self-asserted assurance record
problems.brief: A fabricated record with green flags and a copied population sha passes every assurance check. No evidence digest, commit or figure is re-derived, which V1 did.

problems.title: The certificate harness area does not pin the helper modules its suites import
problems.brief: hybrid_synthetic.py (used by 10 targets) and three other helpers are unpinned. The branch changed hybrid_synthetic.py by 12 lines without moving the certificate.

problems.title: Transfer records compare unit strings and bind neither source record nor instant order
problems.brief: 300 K and 26.85 degC make the provenance unconstructible, which fails closed. Stale and final crossings coexist, and sorting puts iteration 10 before 9, although no production path reaches the stale case.

problems.title: The V3 supersession check passes on any exception
problems.brief: v2_fixtures_still_refused passes even when the rule is removed and an ImportError is raised instead.

problems.title: Parameter identity: the digest and differences() disagree, and unit restatement changes identity
problems.brief: -0.0 and 0.0 show no difference but have different digests. The same bound stated in mV or V is a different identity in 282 of 2000 cases, and the grid-binding helpers have no caller.

problems.title: The exported derive_verdict trusts any object's passed/establishes
problems.brief: A duck-typed check that ValidationReport refuses yields verdict SUPPORTED when passed directly to derive_verdict.

problems.title: FieldTransferContract accepts any verdict
problems.brief: The verdict is never re-derived, so a forged payload or invented fingerprints read COMPATIBLE and may_cross_directly for a 1-to-3 component or kelvin-to-pascal pair.

improvements.title: Router uniqueness contract: no SUPPORTED grid past an unresolved uniqueness caveat, and supplied grids need a uniqueness basis
improvements.brief: Stage 1, now: GLOBAL_UNIQUENESS_NOT_ASSESSED and MULTISTART_INCOMPLETE make step 3 PASSED_OVER, and a GRID_REBUILT record read back with unresolved uniqueness is refused. Stage 2: run any caller MultistartPolicy before accepting a supplied grid, and pass the grid over with GRID_MISSES_A_FOUND_MODE or GRID_UNIQUENESS_NOT_ASSESSED unless it spans the declared bounds. Default to a canonical multistart. This is a V2-symbol behaviour change, so it is additive for V4 on V1.

improvements.title: Adversarial false-confidence conformance suite with pinned reference posteriors
improvements.brief: Turn each verified repro into a case with a dense reference posterior pinned as bytes. Assert invariants: a SUPPORTED 95% interval holds at least 0.90 of the reference mass, the result is equivariant under unit rescaling, and neither zero-information observations nor one-field record edits ever improve the claim. Mark each case xfail and make it strict when its fix lands. Run single-process, and use the suite to select preregistered thresholds.

improvements.title: The credibility report reads the whole result: convergence, declared models and uncertainty
improvements.area: mcp evidence / results uncertainty / sria budget
improvements.brief: Serialize ConvergenceState into the report. Any non-converged state yields INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE through the rule solver_did_not_converge. A provenance override may add models but never drop a result's declared models. Add an uncertainty field that carries source_kind, have uq/predictive produce it, and make the SRIA budget refuse a NUMERICAL record as aleatoric or model_form.

improvements.title: Qualify SUPPORTED where agents read it, and give every verification level an issuer
improvements.area: mcp server verdict block / results validation / mcp evidence
improvements.brief: Put evidence_basis, warning_checks and levels_withheld in the verdict block, key the guidance by (verdict, basis), and add an optional required_evidence_basis. Require a registered reference id and digest for ANALYTICALLY_VERIFIED, as oracle and consensus levels already do. Make the exported derive_verdict accept only ValidationReport, or re-run the level and issuer rules. The response schema is pinned in three places, and the hard benchmark must be re-scored with --workers 4.

improvements.title: Honest multistart: count the search actually performed and classify separated optima by Laplace mass
improvements.brief: Bring max_evaluations and maximum_retractions into the minimum search. Require _minimum_starts(p) converged refits, retrying a failure at the canonical budget. Replace a retracted start with the next Halton point instead of counting it as a full start. A separated converged refit is SECOND_MODE when its Laplace mass ratio exceeds a preregistered floor. Re-check the committed K2 kinetics evidence.

improvements.title: Information-weighted goodness of fit next to the pooled test, plus a small-dof rule
improvements.brief: Add a leverage-weighted residual statistic with a three-moment null. Run it and the pooled test at alpha/2 each and take the worse result. Apply the variance-ratio refusal regardless of p, and give DOWNGRADED GOODNESS_OF_FIT_UNDERPOWERED at dof 1-2. Both need a new preregistered protocol version.

improvements.title: Per-mode grid resolution and admissibility cuts as truncation faces (additive checks, V1 digest unmoved)
improvements.area: inference grid resolution / hybrid_uq grid evidence
improvements.brief: Label basins. Every maximum within ln 1e6 of the peak needs enough nodes, a quadratic fit that passes a residual test, and the aliasing bound, or it gets GRID_MODE_UNRESOLVED. Treat an admissible high-mass node next to an inadmissible one as a truncation face: refuse it on supplied grids and refine there on rebuilds. Also re-apply these checks in routed prediction.

improvements.title: Sound adequacy comparison: full content binding, within-half duplicates, small-n critical values
improvements.brief: Bind split identity, likelihood sigma and twin into content binding, and make content_bound a derived property, not a caller-settable flag. Collapse replicates within a half. Refuse held-out points that match calibration points after unit normalization and rounding. Use a t critical value with n-1 dof and a minimum n before naming a preferred model.

improvements.title: Make the CORE-014 operating-point binding load-bearing by default and bound to the model's conditions
improvements.brief: Add a keyword-only record_values to assess_validity, which is additive on a V1 symbol. Pass it on the DerivedValidityContext, battery, conduction and MCP report paths. Compare evaluated values, including derived conditions, with a tolerance, and keep evaluated in ModelValidityRecord. Refuse an assessment whose satisfied or violated conditions are not the model's, in ScientificResult itself as well as at MCP. Regenerate SHA-pinned fixtures by writing bytes.

improvements.title: Enforce declared validation requirements and uncertainty specs, and parse problems strictly
improvements.brief: from_dict refuses unknown or misspelled keys. Validation requirements must name registered check kinds. When a declared requirement or UncertaintySpecification is unmet, the boundary yields INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE under a named rule. The DC, CSTR and conduction problems then gain real enforcement.

improvements.title: Boundary completeness per edge, not per region id
improvements.brief: Refuse two conditions that share a region id, or key completeness and Dirichlet presence by resolved edge set, so conduction2d cannot silently let the last condition win. Add a production conduction case that declares a duplicate as a regression.

improvements.title: Admit posteriors once: route the production calibration study through the V2 evidence gates
improvements.brief: Add admit_grid plus routed study entry points, record the grid decision per repetition, and deprecate the raw-PosteriorGrid consumers. Add a power floor, giving HELD_OUT_UNDERPOWERED instead of PASS, and cluster-aware coverage intervals. Accept heterogeneous declared sigmas, and record coverage repetitions honestly when no calibration ran. Migrate the TCR and battery B1-B3 audits. Run this after the gates above are sound.

improvements.title: Guard reach ledger with a static bypass check
improvements.brief: Map every guard to the production entry points that reach it, marked REACHED, LIBRARY_ONLY or LATENT with a reason. Fail CI when a REACHED guard loses its path or production calls a known bypass: raw PosteriorGrid consumers, assess_validity without record_values, to_check outside the gate, or route_uncertainty with no multistart plus a rebuild. Audit rows marked FIXED must cite REACHED or LATENT.

improvements.title: Probe redesign: matrix curvature, tails in every relevant direction, unit-invariant basis, counted clipped probes (absorbs former I-17)
improvements.brief: Rebuild the whitened curvature matrix from the existing ±2 sd probes and gate on its extreme eigenvalues. Run tail probes along diagonals and extreme eigenvectors. Build directions from the correlation eigenbasis scaled by marginal sds. Clip probes at bounds, compare with r_clip^2, and count what is skipped. The finding holds. I read the code path, checked the callers, reran the reproduction and ran three variants of my own.

**The code path**
- In local_gaussian.py, lines 1173-1179: once a converged refit is farther away than the separation radius (m2 > chi2.ppf(0.999, p)), its class depends only on its objective. It is SECOND_MODE or BETTER_OPTIMUM only if it lies within chi2.ppf(0.99, p) of the estimate. Anything above that is WORSE_LOCAL_OPTIMUM.
- The rule never looks at the basin's volume or estimated mass.
- `_multistart_verdict` (lines 211-229) never reacts to WORSE_LOCAL_OPTIMUM. It reports uniqueness "MULTISTART_NO_SECOND_MODE" even when every start converged into the other basin.
- `_modes` (the modes a rebuilt grid would cover) also leaves these basins out.
- When a record is read back (lines 537-557), the same rule is applied again, so nothing is caught there either.
- router.py lines 605-607 return a SUPPORTED local result straight away, so no grid is built or checked.

**No other guard catches it**
- The ±2 sd probes and the 3/6 sd tail probes only look inside the narrow mode (nonlinearity 0.003, tail ratio 0.972).
- The goodness-of-fit gate passes.

**Why the confidence is unjustified**
- vocabulary.py says the local route "is a Gaussian approximation of" the posterior.
- The router treats it as interchangeable with a posterior grid under the declared uniform prior (CORE-010).
- Under that prior, the SUPPORTED 95% interval holds only 17% of the posterior mass.
- From a pure likelihood-ratio view the interval would be defensible. It is wrong under the framework's own posterior semantics.

**Not a documented limitation**
- The design doc's "multistart cannot prove uniqueness" covers modes the search misses. Here the search found the basin every time and ignored it, and the record still says no second mode.
- The audit doc does not mention this. The nearest thing is the CORE-003 residual about mass beyond 6 sd escaping the tail probes, which is a different mechanism. So this is new.

**Robustness and reach**
- **Realistic residuals (A):** it still happens with residuals the declared noise explains (chi2/dof 0.38).
- **Narrower bounds (B):** with bounds [-1, 10] instead of [-1, 30], only 16.6% of the posterior mass is inside the interval.
- **Where it stops (C):** it needs a big width ratio. At a chi-square gap of about 9.6 and a width ratio of about 30 (variant C), the interval still holds 86% of the mass.
- **What it takes:** the other basin has to be more than exp(gap/2) times wider than the narrow one. That is plausible for sloppy models, and easier at higher p because the width ratios multiply across dimensions.

**Severity**
P1 rather than P0: it takes a specific geometry, a narrow deep mode beside a broad shallow one. It is still reachable with the default MultistartPolicy and gives a silent SUPPORTED. That matches how the audit rated CORE-003 (P1, an interval holding 4.7% of the mass).

findings.title: Adding observations that carry no information about the parameters dilutes the CORE-001 goodness-of-fit gate: a REFUSED misfit becomes SUPPORTED with an identical covariance
findings.description: _goodness_of_fit tests the pooled chi2_min against chi-square on n - p degrees of freedom. Observations with large declared sigma add almost nothing to J_w'J_w, so they do not change the covariance, but they add degrees of freedom. With properly declared sigma they add about one chi-square unit each; with inflated sigma they add almost none. Ten precise points whose residuals are 3x their sigma refuse MODEL_MISFIT_BEYOND_DECLARED_NOISE on their own. The same ten points plus 60 inflated-sigma points, or plus 1000 correctly declared low-precision points, read SUPPORTED. The covariance agrees to 4 digits in all three cases, so the reported sd is still about 3x too small for the residuals that determine it. Mixed-precision datasets are ordinary, and grid_goodness_of_fit uses the same pooled rule.

- With honest noise, the extra points needed grow roughly with the square of the precise-subset excess chi2. So the sd understatement stays at a few times (below that it hits the ratio-4 refusal) unless N is very large.

findings.description: _posterior_record_problems is the HUQ-12 defence against 'a covariance rescaled everywhere it appears'. That record is also accepted as SUPPORTED, alone and inside a HybridUQResult. The bound-distance check only catches an edit that changes the covariance alone. A forger who keeps the record self-consistent can never be caught, because the Jacobian that anchors the covariance is not stored.

- Stationarity is checked separately, as the Newton step in sd units.

Nothing measured stands behind the downgrade. In my run the optimizer started away from the solution (offset 0.5, slope 1.0 x scale) and still converged. The volt, millivolt, microvolt and nanovolt declarations gave the same slope (2 V), sd (0.0459933105504 V), equilibrated condition (3.474) and chi2 (10). findings.title: The V1 resolution check fits one quadratic about the top node, so an unresolved second mode inside the box passes
findings.description: _grid_resolution_refusal checks ESS, the node count and the tensor lattice. It then fits a single least-squares quadratic to the log-likelihood around the global argmax node and runs the aliasing check on that fit. Nothing checks how well the quadratic fits, and nothing looks at other local maxima of the node log-likelihood. A posterior with a broad main mode and a narrower second mode inside the grid box therefore passes whenever the step resolves the broad mode: the narrow mode's mass is aliased. On an honest supplied grid, every V2 check passes: evidence binding (the grid is exact), goodness of fit, uniform prior and face containment. The result is GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED IDENTIFIABLE with an sd 14x too small. The supplied route returns before the multistart that would find SECOND_MODE_FOUND. The rebuild path aliases the same way when the narrow mode is the multistart-found one; there it overstates the narrow mode's mass and shifts the mean by about 0.3 sd. This is not the CORE-002 residual, which covers modes outside the box.
findings.evidence: calibration.py:699-752 (_fitted_lattice_covariance) fits at top = argmax only, rejects only on singular design, and has no residual or fit-quality test. It floors flat or convex directions to 'cannot alias' (748-751). calibration.py:807-871 applies no per-mode check. Output of r7c_supplied.py (model a(t)*x with a = t^2 for t >= 0 and (8t)^2 for t < 0; modes at +0.99 and -0.124; local sd 0.00519 and 0.00065): step 0.005 gives GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED, narrow-mode mass 0.0005 against true 0.1111, mean error +0.35 sd, sd ratio 0.070, PARAMETERS_IDENTIFIABLE. Step 0.004 gives sd ratio 0.232, IDENTIFIABLE. The grid holds an interior local maximum at -0.1215 that is 7.24 nats below the peak, inside the ln 1e6 band, and is never checked. Output of r7b_scan.py (rebuild path, default multistart): K=9 gives SUPPORTED, narrow mass 0.209 against true 0.100, mean error -0.36 sd.

verification.reason:
I could not refute this finding; the code confirms it. In router.route_uncertainty, step 1 accepts a supplied grid and returns SUPPORTED before the multistart runs. The only resolution check on that path is the V1 check: assess_identifiability calls _grid_resolution_refusal, which calls _fitted_lattice_covariance. That function fits one least-squares quadratic about the argmax node. It never tests how well the quadratic fits, never looks at other local maxima, and treats a flat or convex fit as "cannot alias" (floored to a lattice variance of 1e12). None of the V2 checks look for an interior second mode: evidence binding, prior uniformity, goodness of fit and face containment.

The flaw is worse than the finding says. When nodes from the second mode fall inside the 50-nat fit window, the fitted curvature goes flat, so the aliasing check does not measure even the broad mode. At step 0.015, a grid over the broad mode alone is refused (ESS 1.15). With the second mode inside the box the same step passes: ESS rises to 2.99 and the result is SUPPORTED.

Both halves of the claim reproduce exactly:
- **Supplied grid:** step 0.005 gives SUPPORTED and IDENTIFIABLE, with narrow-mode mass 0.0005 against a true 0.1111 and an sd ratio of 0.070.
- **Rebuild path:** K=9 gives narrow-mode mass 0.209 against 0.100 and a mean error of -0.36 sd.

The finding leaves out that on the rebuild path the verdict is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE and the sd is overstated (ratio 1.36). That half is the milder one.

It is not limited to the finding's half-step grid placement. Ordinary evenly spaced grids fail too:
- `linspace(-0.5, 1.5, 301)` gives SUPPORTED and IDENTIFIABLE with an sd ratio of 0.038. The true posterior is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE (relative width of the 95% interval is 1.30).
- With random grid offsets at step 0.005, 14 of 40 grids give IDENTIFIABLE.
- At width ratios K=3 to 6 on evenly spaced grids, the SUPPORTED moments miss by up to 0.55 to 0.98 sd, and the narrow-mode mass is off by a factor of 2 to 3.

This is not already covered by the audit doc. Its CORE-002 residual covers only modes outside the box, so "new" is right relative to that doc. The gap was, however, noted before. benchmarks/core_v1_thin_ridge_repair/REPAIR_REPORT.md:335 lists "A resolution check that is not a single local quadratic: multimodal ..." as still needing Core V2, and says V1 was validated only on "broad-bimodal shapes". V2 did not add such a check, and its SUPPORTED/IDENTIFIABLE output carries no warning about it. So it is a known gap, but nothing bounds it and the output does not say so.

The route is reachable, nothing later refuses it, and the error is material. I keep P1 rather than P0 because the posterior needs a markedly narrower interior second mode, and the identifiability verdict only flips at large width ratios (about 8x) with unlucky grid alignment.

findings.title: A posterior cut at the declared upper bound, with the data constraining only the lower side, is SUPPORTED, and the declared bound sets its sd
findings.description: CORE-002 retired F1 because its rebuilt sd belonged to the declared upper bound: 1.75, 2.57 and 5.81 with the bound at 20, 40 and 80. The fix passes over GRID_POSTERIOR_BOUND_DOMINATED only when density reaches both declared bounds of an axis. Suppose the data rule out the lower side while the likelihood stays within ln 1e6 of its peak out to the upper declared bound. That posterior is treated as a truncation: steps are halved until the moments stop moving, and the grid is SUPPORTED. Its sd then grows with wherever the bound is declared, which is the exact pathology the fix targeted. With a declared zero far from the posterior (a kelvin-like offset), the verdict is also PARAMETERS_IDENTIFIABLE.

findings.fix_direction: Diagnose bound domination one side at a time. If the log-likelihood profile stays within the ln 1e6 band from the mode all the way to a declared bound, over a span much wider than the fitted local sd, pass over GRID_POSTERIOR_BOUND_DOMINATED. - **The check does work:** with no grinding, the bulk-sharpened grid is refused because one drawn row (5591) is tampered.

- **No grinding still escapes often:** over 2000 random tail nudges, 29.6% escaped (0.312 predicted from 25.3% of nodes tampered).

**Face nodes (containment).** `grid_containment` only looks at usable face nodes, and the spot-check leaves most face nodes unchecked. I took a truncated grid (box of +/-1.5 or +/-2 sd) and marked every face node inadmissible except rows 0 and N-1, with no change to any likelihood value.

- the drawn rows come from supplier bytes, so the check can be ground;

findings.title: Posterior cut by forward-model inadmissibility counts as contained: supplied grids are SUPPORTED with moments off by up to 0.57 sd
findings.description: grid_containment takes each face's peak over admissible nodes only. A posterior cut off by the forward evaluator's refusal inside the box, with all nodes beyond the cut inadmissible, never reaches a face. It passes as contained. The router refuses a supplied grid whose posterior reaches a declared bound face, saying truncated moments cannot be shown to converge, and in a rebuild it halves steps at such a face. The same hard cut made by admissibility gets neither treatment. The V1 aliasing argument assumes a smooth density and does not bound the O(step) error at the cut.
findings.evidence: _grid_evidence.py:122-124: face = (points[:, i] == edge) & usable, face_peak = -inf when no admissible node is on the face. router.py:423 and 464-469 only act on truncation at declared bounds. findings.fix_direction: Treat an admissible node within ln 1e6 of the peak that has an inadmissible lattice neighbour as a truncation face. Refuse it on supplied grids, as at declared bounds, and halve steps across it in the rebuild until the moments converge.

If the forward evaluator refuses everything past a cut inside the box, those faces score -inf and pass. The router's hard-edge handling looks only at declared bounds. A supplied grid is refused when its posterior reaches a declared-bound face (line 126-131). A rebuild halves steps only for faces where abs(edge - bound) <= tol (router.py:464-469). Its ll array is -inf off the admissible nodes (router.py:422-423), so a face cut by admissibility never counts as truncated. findings.title: Grid-route predictions ignore predict and never check the predictive table's values
findings.description: For a LOCAL_GAUSSIAN result the prediction is evaluated through predict. For a grid result, predict is accepted and ignored. The caller's predictive_table is bound to the grid only by parameter names, point coordinates and the admissible mask carrying weight. Its values, which are the prediction, are never compared with any model. HUQ-05 added spot checks for the likelihood table and nothing equivalent covers the predictive table. A table of another model's outputs therefore yields a SUPPORTED prediction.
findings.evidence: router.py:702-715: the grid branch passes predictive_table to _grid_record, and predict is unused. uq/predictive.py:159-177 (_validate_posterior_table_binding) checks names, points and the mask only. Output of r4_predictive_trust.py (a): honest table gives mean 1.9745, param sd 0.0144, SUPPORTED. A table of 2x the model, with predict() passed, gives mean 3.9490, param sd 0.0289, SUPPORTED.
findings.reproduction: <scratch>/hybrid-grid/r4_predictive_trust.py, part (a)
findings.fix_direction: Require predict for grid predictions and verify predictive_table against it at weight-sampled nodes, to SUPPLIED_PREDICTION_AGREEMENT_SD of the spec's scale. Without predict, DOWNGRADE.

verification.reason:
The behaviour is real, but it is less serious than claimed. In router.py:698-715, routed_predictive_uncertainty uses `predict` only on the LOCAL_GAUSSIAN branch. On the grid branch it accepts `predict` and never uses it: a `predict` that raises when called still gives SUPPORTED, and so does predict=None. _grid_record passes the table to the frozen posterior_predictive_uq. That function's _validate_posterior_table_binding (uq/predictive.py) checks only the parameter names, the points and the rejected-mass mask. Nothing checks the table's values, and the audit document does not mention this, so the finding is new.

The claimed consequence is not specific to the grid route. On the LOCAL_GAUSSIAN route `predict` is trusted in exactly the same way. A 2x `predict` shifts the mean from 1.9745 to 3.9490 and the parameter sd from 0.0144 to 0.0289, the same shift as the 2x table, and the claim and reasons stay the same (DOWNGRADED only for GLOBAL_UNIQUENESS_NOT_ASSESSED, a reason unrelated to predict). So a wrong predictive model gets through either route. The core has no independent reference for a new predictive observable to check against: the calibration forward model covers only the calibration observables, and `model` is just a caller-supplied label. The records also state MODEL_DISCREPANCY_NOT_MODELLED. The SUPPORTED claim describes how adequate the posterior approximation is, not whether the caller's predictive model is correct.

The HUQ-05 comparison is also weaker than the finding suggests. That check binds a rebuilt likelihood table to the forward evaluator the route requires for the same observables. Here the only possible reference is `predict`, which the grid route does not require, so a missing cross-check is not a bypass of an existing guard.

What is left is hardening. The grid route should either cross-check the table against `predict` at spot rows when `predict` is given, or refuse a `predict` it will not use, rather than ignore it silently.

findings.title: A calibration_observations set from another dataset silences PREDICTION_OUTSIDE_CALIBRATED_CONDITIONS
findings.description: routed_predictive_uncertainty takes calibration_observations as an unbound keyword argument. Its dataset_id is never compared with the result's dataset (grid_summary.dataset_id or local_posterior.dataset_id), and its content is never compared with the evidence the grid was bound to. Any observation set whose declared conditions cover the prediction lifts the domain downgrade. grid_predictive_uncertainty avoids this by using its content-bound observations for both jobs.

Output of r4_predictive_trust.py (b): prediction at x=5 with the calibration's own conditioned observations gives DOWNGRADED ['PREDICTION_OUTSIDE_CALIBRATED_CONDITIONS']. findings.fix_direction: Refuse calibration_observations whose dataset_id differs from the result's. For grid results, also require its keys and values to match the evidence the grid was bound to, for example through a digest carried in grid_summary.

verification.reason:
I could not refute this. I confirmed it by reading the code and by running my own script.

**The code.** `routed_predictive_uncertainty` (router.py:676-715) accepts `calibration_observations` with no check at all. It sends the value straight on, at line 701 on the local route and at line 712 on the grid route. `_prediction_domain_reasons` (predictive.py:285-308) looks only at `.observations[*].conditions`. Nothing refuses a mismatch:
- Neither function compares the value's `dataset_id` with `result.grid_summary['dataset_id']` or with `result.local_posterior.dataset_id`, though both fields exist on the result.
- Neither compares its content with the evidence the grid or posterior was built from.
- `linearized_predictive_uq` (predictive.py:414) has the same gap.

**Other code does check.** The dataset check is missing only here. Elsewhere the core refuses a dataset mismatch: router.py:528 for a supplied grid, and sensitivity.py:319.

**The record is silent.** `RoutedPredictiveUncertainty` stores nothing about which observation set defined the domain. The only matching key is `observation_key`. A reader of the record cannot audit where the range came from.

**Scope and severity.** The audit document's CORE-006 residual lists three things: the per-condition box, the predictor bound only to the posterior digest, and domains not yet declaring conditions. It does not mention this gap, so "new" is correct. Two points argue against a higher severity:
- `spec.conditions` and `predict`/`predictive_table` are also taken on trust from the caller, so a caller set on getting SUPPORTED could simply declare an in-range condition. This finding mainly adds a silent honest-mistake route, such as passing a pooled, validation or other dataset.

P2, a silently weakened guard, fits.

findings.title: Grid result read-back re-derives less than it claims: covariance shrink, identifiability flip and an impossible rebuild record all read back
findings.description: For grid decisions, read-back holds the identifiability report to the carried covariance. It also bounds each relative width from above by a Cantelli interval. First, the covariance alone can be divided by about 8 with only the integrity-only moments digest recomputed. Second, widths are only upper-bounded, so lowering them with the covariance allows any shrink, and lowering them alone turns NOT_IDENTIFIABLE into IDENTIFIABLE. ESS and spacing_to_std are never held to anything. Third, a GRID_REBUILT record may carry a local posterior with MODEL_MISFIT_BEYOND_DECLARED_NOISE, which contradicts the batch-1 statement 'No grid route, supplied or rebuilt, is used past either. Re-derived on read'. Fourth, 'considered' is never checked, so () is accepted.

- A node that fails it raises `HybridUQError`. It is not recorded as PASSED_OVER.
- So one mismatched spot-check node aborts the whole request, including a local route that would have succeeded.

- With a constant relative bias of 1e-9 (about 1e-5 sd per residual), the request raises.

**Limits on the claim.**
- It only triggers when the grid's values differ from a fresh forward evaluation. A grid built by the same deterministic evaluator always passes. Realistic sources are warm-started iterative solvers, nondeterministic parallel or BLAS code, or a grid computed with a different build or on another machine.
- At 1e-5 sd per residual, whether it fires depends on how the error correlates with the residuals. The constant bias and the finder's random per-call noise trigger it. A fixed cos pattern and a fixed random pattern do not.
- The failure is loud (an exception), not a silent wrong conclusion. It weakens no guard, and the caller can retry without the grid.

**New or residual.** The audit document's CORE-005 row says a mismatch raises `HybridUQError`. It does not mention that the 1e-6 sd tolerance rejects a grid that differs only at solver-tolerance level, or that the raise stops the local route from running. "New" is fair.

I tried to refute this and could not. The finding holds, but the effect only becomes material when a caller supplies a box much smaller than the posterior.

- **No containment check on the frozen path.** `posterior_predictive_uq` (`uq/predictive.py:237-361`) checks only that the table matches the posterior, then applies `_grid_resolution_refusal` with the discrete waiver. Neither checks containment: `calibration.py:807-871` looks only at ESS, node count, the lattice and aliasing. A grep for edge/face/contain/truncat finds nothing in `inference/grid.py`, `calibration.py`, `split.py`, `uq/` or `adequacy/`. `grid_containment` is called only in `hybrid_uq/predictive.py:125`, `hybrid_uq/router.py:580` and `_grid_evidence.py:174`.
- **Content binding does not cover the box.** `assess_predictive_observation` binds by recomputing the log-likelihood on the posterior's own nodes (`split.py:416-423`). A truncated box has exactly that likelihood on its nodes, so it passes as `content_bound`.
- **The comparison has no containment gate.** `compare_log_predictive_scores` gates on `content_bound`, n >= 2, |delta| > 4 and 2 standard errors, and nothing else. It is the only place a preferred model is named.
- **The study functions add none either.** `validate_held_out` and `predict_held_out` add content binding, a check that the declared sigma is used, and the TCR physics-validity check. They do not add containment or a calibrated-range check.

- Routed containment refuses any box of ±5 sd or narrower.
- The frozen comparison stays non-decisive (delta 2.87 to 3.74) down to ±1.5 sd. At ±1 sd it becomes decisive (delta 4.97, se 1.72, prefers A), and at ±0.6 sd delta is 6.26.
- An off-centre box [-0.3, +1.5] sd gives delta 8.69, preferring A.

The TCR study shows the same thing. With a ±0.6 se grid, which routed containment refuses, it still returns PASS and 3/3 covered. Parameter sd drops to 0.40x at 310 K, 0.77x at 350 K and 0.60x at 420 K. The 420 K prediction lies outside the calibrated 300-400 K range, and nothing in the record says so.

- It needs a caller-supplied box narrower than about ±1 sd. The study's own builders (±6 se in the tests, and `_bounded_axis` in the coverage study) are contained.
- The frozen record makes no SUPPORTED-type claim about the domain; it just leaves the qualifier out.
- It is a CORE-002/CORE-006 gate that was not applied to the adequacy, comparison and study paths, which fits P2.

Residual or new: mostly new.
- The CORE-002 residual in the audit document names only the second-mode case and the one-bound case.
- The CORE-006 residual does not mention the frozen or study predictions.
- The CORE-007 and CORE-011 residuals do not mention containment.

The finding holds; I could not refute it. In src/engcore/scientific/results/validation.py (commit 294c129), comparison_met_its_bound (lines 99-105) turns both numbers into floats, checks only that they are finite, and returns `residual <= tolerance`. Nothing checks the sign or takes abs(). So a PASS with residual=-10 (or -1e300) against tolerance 1e-6 is built, survives the to_dict/from_dict round trip, reports status=pass and carries its level. A negative tolerance is also accepted. A WARNING that declares a level gets through the same way. The audit doc says nothing about signed residuals or GUARD 21, so "new" is the right label.

It stays P3, for three reasons:
1. The core and domain code that builds these checks always passes a non-negative residual: abs() differences in lumped.py and oracles.py, abs residual over tolerance in conservation.py, abs(absorbed) in dc validation. No normal path produces a signed residual.
2. GUARD 21 only checks that a hand-written outcome agrees with its own numbers; it is not an authority barrier. The same caller can get the same PASS and level by leaving out the numbers and passing any evidence string, e.g. evidence=("anything",).

findings.description: CrossSolverConsensus.to_check reports FAIL for a disagreement only when routes_are_independent holds. Independence is what makes agreement confirmatory, and it is irrelevant to refutation. findings.title: Oracle absolute tolerance on an interval scale is converted as an absolute temperature
findings.description: An oracle's absolute_tolerance is a difference, but both the constructor and compare convert it with magnitude_in(expected.units), which is an affine conversion. A tolerance written '0.5 degC' against an expected value in kelvin becomes 273.65 K, so a prediction 273 K off PASSes. With the identity pinned, it earns EXPERIMENTALLY_VALIDATED. Mixed degF/degC does the same (30 degF off passes a '1 degC' band). The opposite spelling is refused: a legitimate 0.5 kelvin band on an expected value in degC converts to -272.65 degC and fails 'tolerance must be non-negative'. The repository already refuses tolerances and differences on affine scales elsewhere (is_ratio_scale in units/quantity.py cites a coupling tolerance and an excursion span), but this record does not. Latent in production: no oracle is pinned and nothing outside the core builds OracleEvidenceSet. It is the designed route to experimental validation.

findings.title: Oracle operating-point conditions are the caller's word, partial, and optional
findings.description: The CORE-009 fix compares an observation only at its declared conditions, but those conditions are checked against the conditions= argument of compare, not against the prediction. predicted is a plain Mapping[str, Quantity] with no provenance, so a caller whose prediction was computed at 400 K passes conditions={'T': 300 K} and gets PASS, with the level too once the oracle is pinned. Two further gaps: stated conditions the observation does not declare are ignored silently (an observation at T only is compared against a prediction at P = 50 bar), and an observation with no conditions, like every record written before the field existed, compares at any operating point. The audit's stated residual covers check-to-result binding and pins without conditions. It does not cover the fact that the comparison itself takes the operating point on assertion. Latent in production, as no oracle is pinned.
findings.evidence: oracles.py:382-411 (stated = dict(conditions or {}); only observation.conditions keys are compared; predicted is never consulted for its operating point). Output of r1_oracle.py: B 'outcome with stated T=300 K: pass' (no link to where y was computed); B2 (observation at T only, stated P=50 bar) 'outcome: pass'; B3 (observation without conditions, stated T=9999 K) 'outcome: pass'.
findings.reproduction: r1_oracle.py sections B, B2, B3.
findings.fix_direction: Take the operating point from the prediction's own record: accept a ScientificResult or a provenance mapping and read the conditions from provenance.inputs, the same way ScientificResult binds CORE-014. Refuse a pinned oracle whose observations declare no conditions for EXPERIMENTALLY_VALIDATED. Consider requiring that the stated operating point covers every input the result's provenance records, rather than ignoring extras.

verification.reason:
The behaviour is real, but the harm is smaller than claimed and most of it is already listed as a residual.

What the code does (src/engcore/scientific/oracles.py:395-411):
- compare builds `stated = dict(conditions or {})` and loops only over each observation's own `conditions` keys.
- It never looks at `predicted` to find the operating point. Even when `predicted` contains T=400 K, a call stating 300 K passes.
- Conditions the caller states that the observation doesn't declare are ignored without a word.
- An observation with no conditions is compared at any stated operating point.
- A passing record's evidence tuple (lines 452-462) does not say which operating point the comparison was made at, and `_oracle_issuer_gap` (validation.py:320-358) does not ask for one. So the level survives into `ValidationReport.attained_levels`.

Why P3 rather than P2:
1. **Latent.** `_TRUSTED_ORACLE_DECLARATIONS` is empty (size 0) and nothing under src/ calls `OracleEvidenceSet.compare`. No level can be awarded in production today.
2. **No new attack surface.** `predicted` is an unprovenanced mapping too. A caller can pass the expected values plus the conditions copied from the evidence and get a pass with the level, with or without the conditions check. The conditions check guards against honest mistakes, not adversaries. Tying conditions to `predicted` would not close anything unless the check were also bound to the result.
3. **Mostly residual.** The audit's CORE-009 row is marked PARTIAL. Its residuals are: "A `ValidationCheck` is still not bound to the result it qualifies (the deferred VAL-01 field)" and "no pinned oracle declares conditions yet". The first covers the main claim (B), because binding the check to the result's inputs is what would supply the real operating point. The second partly covers B3.
4. **B2 is arguable.** Ignoring extra stated conditions is a reasonable meaning for "the observation declares its operating point".

What is new, and it is minor: a passing oracle check doesn't record the operating point it was compared at, and a pinned observation with no conditions adds no warning. Both weaken how the result is communicated, not the guard itself.

findings.title: CrossLimitCondition reports a missing declaration as a core gap whenever one operand is supplied
findings.description: CrossLimitCondition.explain_in asks _absent_or_unreadable of each operand and returns UNREADABLE_SHAPE if either answer is UNREADABLE_SHAPE. _absent_or_unreadable returns UNREADABLE_SHAPE for any value that is not None, including a perfectly readable Quantity. So whenever one limit is declared and the other omitted, the reason is UNREADABLE_SHAPE ('a gap in the core, the caller can do nothing about it') instead of NOT_SUPPLIED. That is the common case for the production RATED_LINEAR_TCR_MODEL: reference_temperature is always declared and maximum_operating_temperature and debye_temperature are optional. domains.repair then tells the user 'Declaring it again will not help: the gap is in the core', and actionable_declarations drops the condition. The reason channel also over-counts core-universality gaps. unknown_diagnostics has the same blind spot: _context_key falls back to the condition name, which a cross-limit condition never reads, so the diagnostic names a nonexistent key and reports UNSPECIFIED_UNREADABLE_VALUE.
findings.evidence: definition.py:137-155 (_absent_or_unreadable: any non-None value is UNREADABLE_SHAPE), 668-685 (CrossLimitCondition.explain_in). unknown_diagnostics.py:126-135. repair.py:997-1001. Output of r7_crosslimit_reason.py on mat.RATED_LINEAR_TCR_MODEL's reference_temperature_utilization: 'status: unknown | reason: unreadable_shape' / 'repair guidance: False - ... Declaring it again will not help: the gap is in the core, not in the declaration' / 'actionable declarations: ()' / 'with neither operand: not_supplied | actionable: ('reference_temperature_utilization',)'. Output of r6_struct_diag.py S2: 'unspecified_unreadable_value | context_key: ref_below_max'.
findings.reproduction: r7_crosslimit_reason.py: ValidityDomain(conditions=(the reference_temperature_utilization condition,)).assess({'reference_temperature': Quantity(293.15,'kelvin')}) then domains.repair.unassessable_guidance.
findings.fix_direction: In CrossLimitCondition.explain_in, return UNREADABLE_SHAPE only for an operand that is present and not a Quantity; if every present operand is a Quantity, return NOT_SUPPLIED. In unknown_diagnostics, key cross-limit diagnostics on the missing operand (numerator or denominator), not on the condition label.

verification.reason:
The finding is real, and I could not refute it.

**Code.** In `definition.py`:
- `_absent_or_unreadable` (lines 137-155) returns `UNREADABLE_SHAPE` for any value that is not None. A perfectly readable `Quantity` counts.
- `CrossLimitCondition.explain_in` (lines 668-685) returns `UNREADABLE_SHAPE` if either operand gets that answer.

`ValidityDomain.assess` (line 1468) calls `explain_in` whenever `evaluate_in` returns UNKNOWN. So for this condition type, supplying one operand and omitting the other always records `unreadable_shape`, never `not_supplied`.

**Downstream effects.**
- `repair.unassessable_guidance` maps that reason to actionable=False with the text "Declaring it again will not help: the gap is in the core".
- `actionable_declarations` drops the condition.
- `UnknownCondition.is_actionable` is False.
- `diagnose_unknowns` uses `_context_key`, which falls back to the condition's own name. That key is never read, so even the correct NOT_SUPPLIED case says "context contains no value for 'reference_temperature_utilization'".
- The reason is carried into results (`result.py:611`) and into MCP evidence aggregation.

**Normal production path.** I used the real `build_resistance_problem` and `assess_rated_resistance_validity` with a conductor that declares only `linearization_band`. Both `reference_temperature_utilization` and `reference_reduced_debye_temperature` came back `unreadable_shape` with core-gap guidance. The sibling single-key conditions missing the same declarations were correctly `not_supplied`.

**Nothing elsewhere corrects it.** Outside `repair.py` and `unknown_diagnostics.py`, nothing branches on the reason. It is not mentioned in `CORE_SCIENTIFIC_AUDIT_2026-09-16.md` (only CORE-018's bound ordering touches cross-limit), so the "new" label holds.

**Why P3 rather than P2.** The status stays UNKNOWN, and no verdict or gate reads the reason. The bug never produces more confidence than the evidence supports, and it removes no justified conclusion; the condition really is unassessable. What goes wrong is the stored reason and the repair advice: a missing declaration is labelled a core gap and dropped from the "what to declare" list. That misleads the user but weakens no guard. P2 is arguable because the wrong reason is stored in results, but P3 fits the rubric better.

findings.title: Consensus verdict depends on route order through the 'first reporting route's unit' rule
findings.description: CORE-018 converts every route's value to the unit of the first declared route that reports the name. Two unit-dependent parts of the comparison then depend on declaration order. (a) Declared absolute floors (<key>.floor.<kind>) are bare floats read 'in the unit the routes report that kind in', so the same two readings (0 A and 5e-13 mA) agree and earn CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED in one order and disagree in the other. (b) relative_difference is taken on whatever scale the first route used, so on an affine unit (degC against kelvin) the ratio has no fixed meaning and the level flips with order. The unit layer already has is_ratio_scale for this; CrossLimitCondition uses it and _compare does not. The from_results docstring still says values are read 'in its own unit, so a route that returned the right number in another unit shows up as a disagreement', which the code no longer does. Not currently reachable with production pins: DC fixes native-first and reports volts and amperes, and the kinetics pins are not independent.
findings.evidence: consensus.py:1895-1937 (common_unit.setdefault from the first route), 740-769 (floors are unit-less floats), 721-729 (relative_difference on raw magnitudes). Output of r5_consensus_units.py (synthetic routes pinned beside the production pins via tests/route_declarations_for_tests, DC_CONSENSUS_THRESHOLDS): H1 'routes ['a', 'b']: worst=5e-10 agreed=True establishes=ValidationLevel.CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED' / 'routes ['b', 'a']: worst=5e-07 agreed=False establishes=None'. H2 'routes ['a', 'b']: worst=9.999e-05 agreed=False establishes=None' / 'routes ['b', 'a']: worst=3.661e-10 agreed=True establishes=ValidationLevel.CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED'.
findings.reproduction: r5_consensus_units.py.
findings.fix_direction: Give floors a unit in the threshold declaration, or compare in a canonical unit per dimension (base unit), independent of route order. Refuse, or convert to the base unit, relative comparisons of quantities on an affine scale. Update the from_results docstring.

verification.reason:
I could not refute this finding. The code does what the finding says. In `CrossSolverConsensus.from_results` (consensus.py:1897-1900), `common_unit.setdefault(name, quantity.units)` takes each quantity's unit from whichever declared route reports it first. Every route's value is then converted to that unit (line 1935). `_compare` then applies two unit-dependent rules to those converted numbers:
- **Floors:** the declared floor is a bare float (`_declared_floors`, 740-749) used as `floor / tolerance` in `_floored_difference` (768), so it is read in whatever unit came first.
- **Relative difference:** `relative_difference` (721-729) divides raw magnitudes and never checks `is_ratio_scale`, which exists in units/quantity.py:610.

Nothing later catches this:
- `_require_the_comparison_follows_from_its_numbers` recomputes from `reported_values`, but those numbers are already converted, so a reloaded record agrees with itself.
- `establishes` awarded the level in both orderings.

The flip works in both directions:
- **Too strict:** mA listed first, or degC near 0, refuses an agreement that should pass.
- **Too loose:** megaampere listed first makes the 1e-15 floor worth 1e-9 A, so a 5e-10 A difference on a zero current earns `CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED`; the reverse order refuses it. degC at -200 listed first also passes a pair that the kelvin-first order refuses.

The `from_results` docstring (1877-1880) still says each quantity is read "in its own unit", which the code no longer does. It is new rather than residual: the audit document describes CORE-018 as fixed with first-route-unit conversion and says nothing about order, floors or affine scales.

Severity stays P3 because I found no production path to it. The only caller of `from_results` in src is dc_consensus.py:330. It always lists the native route first, and the DC routes report on the same ratio scales. Reaching the flip needs a different caller that mixes units across routes (the reproduction uses test pins beside the production pins).

findings.title: Oracle comparison scores an unpredicted metric as FAIL and can never compare a multi-point evidence set
findings.description: A metric the observations contain but the prediction mapping lacks is recorded as a failure ('z:missing'), so the check is FAIL, which derive_verdict reads as NOT_SUPPORTED. No comparison was made. This is the evidence-against-by-absence reading that CORE-009 and CORE-013 moved to NOT_RUN. In the other direction, observations inside one set must have unique metrics, and compare requires a single stated operating point that matches every observation's conditions. A set holding observations at more than one operating point (the normal shape of an experimental dataset) is therefore always NOT_RUN, and the same metric cannot appear at two points. Justified comparisons are lost.
findings.evidence: oracles.py:298-300 (metrics unique), 395-411 (one stated point must match every observation), 416-419 (missing becomes a failure), 448 and 477 (FAIL). Output of r1_oracle.py D: 'outcome: fail oracle comparison failed: ['z:missing']'. E (observations at T=300 K and T=400 K): 'stated T=300.0: not_run' / 'stated T=400.0: not_run'.
findings.reproduction: r1_oracle.py sections D and E.
findings.fix_direction: Report metrics without a prediction as NOT_RUN or incomplete, not FAIL. Key observations by (metric, operating point), and compare each observation against predictions made at its own conditions (a mapping of operating point to prediction), awarding a level only when all were compared and passed.

verification.reason:
Both behaviours are real in src/engcore/scientific/oracles.py and I reproduced them. P3 is the right severity, but the second half of the finding overstates the harm.

1) A metric the prediction leaves out is scored as a failure. Lines 416-419 add 'z:missing' to the failures list, and lines 448 and 477 then make the check FAIL. derive_verdict (mcp/evidence.py:648) turns any FAIL into NOT_SUPPORTED before it looks at NOT_RUN. So leaving a metric out gives NOT_SUPPORTED, while stating every metric at the wrong operating point gives only INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. That is inconsistent with the CORE-009 NOT_RUN rule, and with derive_verdict's own rule that an omission is a gap, not a finding.

2) One evidence set can only be compared at one operating point:
- Metrics must be unique within a set (lines 298-300).
- compare takes a single conditions mapping, and every observation's declared conditions must match it (lines 395-411).
- A set whose observations were made at different conditions is therefore NOT_RUN whatever is stated, even with no conditions stated at all.

The finding overstates this part:
- Splitting the data into one set per operating point works; both halves PASS.
- The cost is one identity, and one registry pin, per point. Justified comparisons are not lost outright.
- Nothing fails silently: the detail text explains the NOT_RUN, although its wording is misleading when the prediction is at one of the observed points.

Why P3 and not higher:
- Neither behaviour can raise confidence. Both only lower a verdict.
- Nothing in src/ calls OracleEvidenceSet.compare.
- _TRUSTED_ORACLE_DECLARATIONS is empty, so no set can earn a level.

One side effect makes an adoption gap: the easy way to fit a multi-point dataset into a single set is to put the point in the metric name and drop the conditions. That passes at any stated operating point (output F), which quietly skips the CORE-009 binding.

New or residual: new. The audit doc's residuals for CORE-009 and CORE-013 mention neither the missing-metric FAIL nor the one-point-per-set limit.

findings.title: Validity condition primitives accept declarations whose meaning silently inverts
findings.description: (a) CategoryCondition(allowed='laminar'), and from_dict with 'allowed': 'laminar', store frozenset of the characters {'a','i','l','m','n','r'}. 'laminar' is then OUTSIDE_VALIDATED_DOMAIN and 'a' is IN_DOMAIN. The module refuses exactly this bare-string shape for RangeCondition.requires. (b) CrossLimitCondition bounds numerator/denominator. It moves interval-scale operands to the base unit but never requires ratio-scale operands to be positive, so for sign-indefinite quantities 'a/b <= 1' is not 'a <= b': a = -0.5 V, b = -1 V is IN_DOMAIN although a > b, and a = 2 V, b = -1 V is IN_DOMAIN too. Current production use is temperatures in kelvin, so this is not reached today.
findings.evidence: definition.py:458-466 and 505 (frozenset(self.allowed) and frozenset(payload.get('allowed', ()))), 731-743 (ratio with no sign requirement). Output of r3_validity.py V6: 'allowed stored as: ['a', 'i', 'l', 'm', 'n', 'r']' / ''laminar' -> outside_validated_domain | 'a' -> in_domain'. V5: 'a=-0.5 V, b=-1.0 V (a<=b is False): in_domain' / 'a=2.0 V, b=-1.0 V (a<=b is False): in_domain'.
findings.reproduction: r3_validity.py sections V5 and V6.
findings.fix_direction: Refuse str or bytes for allowed in the constructor and in from_dict. Require CrossLimitCondition operands to be strictly positive on their base unit, or refuse a non-positive denominator or numerator with a ModelValidityError, as a zero denominator is already refused.

verification.reason:
I tried to refute both halves and could not. Both are real, and P3 is the right severity.

(a) CategoryCondition.__post_init__ (definition.py:462) calls frozenset(self.allowed), and from_dict (line 505) calls frozenset(payload.get('allowed', ())). Neither checks the type. So a bare string like 'laminar' is split into single characters. That shape still gets through ValidityDomain construction and assessment, and to_dict writes the character list back out, so a round trip keeps the corruption. The same module refuses this exact shape for RangeCondition.requires with a ModelValidityError, so the two are inconsistent. The effect on the intended value is fail-closed: 'laminar' comes out OUTSIDE_VALIDATED_DOMAIN. It fails open only when the context value is a single character from that set.

(b) When both units are ratio-scale, CrossLimitCondition.evaluate_in (lines 731-743) divides the magnitudes with no check on sign. So 'numerator/denominator <= 1' does not mean 'numerator <= denominator' for signed operands. The arithmetic itself is correct. The gap is that the primitive exists to state one declared limit against another, and with negative operands the ratio stops working as that ordering. Quantity also accepts negative kelvin: -10 K over -20 K is reported IN_DOMAIN.

Neither half is reachable in production today. No module under src/ uses CategoryCondition. The only CrossLimitCondition users are the three in domains/electrical/material.py, and they compare temperatures that the material constructor requires to be positive (checks at material.py:1062, 1180, 1448, 1475). So this is hardening of public API primitives and belongs at P3, not a trust gap on a normal path.
